points.description: Defines DHCP as a network management protocol in IP networks in which a DHCP server dynamically assigns IP addresses (and other network configuration parameters) to devices/hosts on the network. Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says it assigns IP addresses automatically without mentioning server or other configuration parameters is still full; award 0.25 if the definition is vague (e.g. 'a protocol for network configuration') without dynamic IP assignment.

points.description: States what it is used for: simplifies installation/configuration of end systems, supports manual and automatic IP assignment, and/or provides additional configuration info such as DNS server, netmask, default router (at least one such use given). Mentioning that it replaced RARP/BOOTP is also acceptable.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.25 if only a vague use is given without a specific example from the model answer.
